answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may vote on reputation or claim work. The protocol weights influence by stake, then slashes tokens when a randomly sampled task is shown to be fraudulent, using signed evidence and an appeal window. Splitting one stake across a hundred Sybil identities does not multiply voting power; each new identity needs more capital, while cheating risks losing it. A lantern dashboard on the mesa might expose the kernel of this rule: identities are cheap, credible weight is not.
